summary:
We developed Mars Outpost, a free browser-based simulation game. Players manage a crew of four astronauts during a 178-sol mission in Jezero Crater. To survive, they generate oxygen, extract subsurface ice for water, cultivate food, maintain solar panels and repair failing systems. The game also recreates real events documented by NASA, such as the 2018 global dust storm and the 2024 solar storm. To complete the mission, players must produce enough rocket propellant to return to Earth.

Every mechanic is grounded in NASA research. When an event occurs, the game explains the real science behind it. As a result, players come to understand why astronauts never conduct solo spacewalks, why Martian dust is hazardous, and why communication with Earth is delayed by up to 22 minutes.

This project matters because few people grasp the real challenges of living on Mars. By making authentic science interactive and accessible, Mars Outpost aims to inspire the next generation of scientists and engineers.
details:
Mars Outpost is a browser survival game where you lead four astronauts through 178 sols in Jezero Crater. Players make oxygen, drill buried ice for water, grow food, clean dusty solar panels and repair systems. They also have to survive real events like the 2018 dust storm and the 2024 solar storm, and produce enough rocket fuel to launch home. A guided mission list and an arrow teach each step, and a “Real Mars” panel explains the NASA science behind it.

The game turns NASA research into hands-on learning: why astronauts never go out alone, why Mars dust is dangerous, and why messages from Earth take up to 22 minutes. It’s free, runs in any browser, and every fact links to a NASA source. Our goal is to spark interest in space science among young people, especially in Latin America. The game also explains honestly that a real mission would last about 500 days, not six months.

We built it with TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML5 Canvas and the Web Audio API. It’s hosted on GitHub Pages. We prototyped it in Google AI Studio and used Claude to help with code and research.
